name: fireside-interior-v1
scope: The product's own screens and letters: backstage, portal, public event pages, and every string that leaves in an inbox. NOT the marketing page, which has its own bank (deslop skill, taste-bank-v1.1.json).
established: 2026-08-17, from three critic passes over the interior (waves 1-3).

hard_rules.says: Name the domain in the words an organizer already owns: assign, assignment, reviewer, proposal, decision, letter. Never hand out / holding / reader / the pile as unexplained metaphor.
hard_rules.why: The review room spoke a house dialect that was coherent to its builders and a riddle to everyone else: 'Hand out again — it only gives out what nobody holds'.

hard_rules.says: An empty state states its one fact and stops. Mechanics belong on the control that performs them, said once.
hard_rules.why: The proposal page explained the portal twice on one screen: once in the empty rail, once on the form beneath it.

hard_rules.says: Never assert a cause, a feeling, or a count the software cannot know. State what happened.
hard_rules.why: A rejection read 'There were more proposals than the days have hours' — consolation the product cannot verify.

hard_rules.says: The load-bearing noun lives in the sentence, not in the surrounding chrome. A line must survive being read alone, in a screenshot or an inbox.
hard_rules.why: 'The committee did not choose this one' names nothing; a speaker with two proposals could not tell which died.

hard_rules.says: One word per object across every surface. The public program is 'the program' everywhere, not schedule/agenda/program/speaker page by turns.
hard_rules.why: 'room' meant venue room, recipient cohort, and quota slot on three screens.

hard_rules.says: Never surface the demo's or the schema's internals in product copy. No 'real addresses', no 'picker', no table names.
hard_rules.why: A send confirm said 'real addresses get an email too', implying some speakers are fake.

hard_rules.says: A letter is signed by whoever actually sent it. Conference business signs as the conference; only sign-in and check-in links sign as Fireside.
hard_rules.why: A committee's decision arriving 'sent from Fireside' hands the reader a vendor at the moment they most want a person.

hard_rules.says: Em and en dashes are permitted in interior copy. The marketing bank's ban does not extend here.

accepted.line: Marks stay yours until you submit them.
accepted.why: Removes the reviewer's actual fear in six words.

accepted.line: If you did not ask for it, ignore this and nothing happens.
accepted.why: Plain, calm, and true at a suspicious moment.

accepted.line: Nothing is asked of you until then.
accepted.why: Kills the waitlisted speaker's main anxiety, literally.
Names the product's central promise in five words.

accepted.line: Only the person writing it can see what is in it.
accepted.why: States visibility unprompted, which almost nothing does.
An empty state that says the fact the reader came for.

accepted.line: Your slides are in. The organizers can see them from here on.

rejected.line: Nothing is being asked of them yet. Ask below and it lands on their portal against this proposal.
Hand out again — it only gives out what nobody holds
Anyone already holding one keeps it.
There were more proposals than the days have hours, and the committee read every one of them.
The committee did not choose this one for {event}.
They land in the speakers' portals at once, and real addresses get an email too.
Everything about your talk is in your portal.
rejected.note: An absolute the product cannot guarantee.

rejected.line: Nothing has gone out. Read them before they do.
The committee has moved this talk on, so it can no longer be withdrawn here.
rejected.note: 'moved on' could mean accepted, declined or advanced.

conference_truths: A decision is staged as a letter and reaches nobody until a human releases the outbox.
A reviewer's marks are private until they submit them.
Blind rounds hide names from reviewers, never from the chair.
The nightly rebuild resets the demonstration conferences only; a real sign-in's work is never touched.
Speakers with synthetic @example.org addresses get portal messages but no email.

process.writer_critic_separation: The critic never sees the writer's rationale and generates its own literal paraphrase first. Run each pass with a fresh critic context.
process.two_diseases: Wave 1's disease (jargon, lectures) is not wave 2's (missing antecedents, leaked plumbing). A critic told to look for one will certify a page carrying the other. Vary the grudge.
process.stop_rule: Fix bugs and confusions; do not churn copy nobody has complained about. Rewriting healthy text costs more than it returns.
